normalization: The Archive's OCR text layer (_djvu.txt) of the whole volume, line endings normalized; the scan is held by reference with the Archive's md5. The OCR is kept as made, with line endings normalized. No text was corrected by hand; the loci keep the OCR's readings and say where those differ from the printed page.
scope: The volume's OCR layer entire: the Presocratics, Ocellus, Timaeus Locrus and the Pythagorean fragments in Mullach's Greek and Latin. The seat is held for the writings under Archytas's name, above all the book on the ten categories (Περὶ τῶν καθόλου λόγων, the καθολικοὶ λόγοι δέκα), which Simplicius (seated in aristotle-commentators, 31/04) takes as Archytas's and as the source Aristotle followed. Thesleff's The Pythagorean Texts of the Hellenistic Period (1965) and Szlezák's Pseudo-Archytas über die Kategorien (1972) are in copyright and go to 32/11.
verified_loci: Mullach's heading for the Archytan fragments — 'ARCHYT/E TARENTINI' (the page reads ARCHYTAE; the OCR reads ARCHYT/E)
C. Logica: the book on the ten categories, in Mullach's Latin — 'De decem Categoriis liber.'

the categories book opens: five things belong to every art, matter, instrument, part, definition and end — 'materia , instrumentum, pars, definilio et finis.' (the page reads definitio; the OCR reads definilio)

Mullach on fifteen passages from the pseudo-Archytan book called the καθολικοὶ λόγοι δέκα, passed off as Ocellus — 'quindecim loca, e Pseudarchytz libro qui in- scribitur' (the page reads Pseudarchytae; the OCR reads Pseudarchytz)
Mullach: the letter of Plato to Archytas is spurious — 'nem. Nam spuria est Platonis ad Archytam'
why_seated: The pseudo-Archytan Categories is the case where the slot of the one name runs the other way: a book in Doric under an older name, read by the Neoplatonist commentators as Aristotle's source. The study reads it beside Simplicius's proof of the Categories' genuineness.
